newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean parliament hits Tokyo over boat seizure.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean parliament hits Tokyo over boat seizure.

text.p: South Korea's parliament on Thursday lashed out at Japan for the seizure of Korean fishing boats in disputed waters, and demanded an apology and compensation.
The 299-member parliament unanimously adopted a resolution calling for the immediate release of two detained South Korean captains and steps to prevent the repetition of "such illegal acts".
"We urge the Japanese government to apologise to the government and people of the Republic of Korea and compensate for the damage wrought by the illegal abduction," it said.

Japanese patrol boats captured five fishing boats in the past several weeks in waters recently claimed by Tokyo. All five boats and their crew members, except the captains of two vessels, have been released.

"The Republic of Korea National Assembly regards this illegal act as one that damages the trust that has been built up between the two countries through good neighbourly relations and hereupon expresses deep regret over it," the resolution said.

Japan and South Korea are currently negotiating new fisheries agreements, and Seoul argues that the existing agreement, which has been in force for more than 30 years, must be observed until a revision is worked out.
Japan in January expanded its territorial waters following a new maritime convention introduced by the United Nations in November 1994.

"The straight baseline unilaterally drawn up by Japan to define its territorial waters cannot be recognised because part of the baseline is arbitrarily drawn on the basis of points that do not agree with the provisions of the pertinent international laws," the South Korean parliament said.
Earlier this month, South Korean Vice Foreign Minister Lee Ki-choo called in the Japanese ambassador in Seoul, Shintaro Yamashita, to lodge a formal protest over the seizures.
Tensions have frequently risen over territorial claims between Japan and South Korea, which have maintained uneasy relations since the end of Japan's 1910-45 colonisation of the Korean peninsula.
